# Terraform AWS Lambda Deployment Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy/commits)


Terraform module that deploys an AWS Lambda function from a packaged artifact stored in S3, together with
everything it needs to run: IAM roles and policies, a CloudWatch log group, optional VPC and EFS attachment,
Function URLs, aliases, EventBridge schedules, and S3/SQS/DynamoDB event source triggers. The module is driven
by a single structured `lambda` variable and is designed to be consumed through Terragrunt within the
CloudOps Works hub-and-spoke landing zone.


---

This project is part of our comprehensive approach towards DevOps Acceleration.

## Introduction

The AWS Lambda Deployment Module is a comprehensive Terraform solution for deploying and managing AWS Lambda
functions from CI/CD pipelines. The deployment package is read from an S3 versions bucket, and every resource is
named consistently from the release name, the namespace, and the organization/environment coordinates supplied by
the Terragrunt hierarchy.

Key capabilities:

| Capability | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Function deployment | Deploys a `Zip` package from S3, publishes a new version on every apply, and renders the release version into the function description. |
| Runtime tuning | Memory, timeout, reserved concurrency, provisioned concurrency, and ephemeral `/tmp` storage. |
| IAM | A default execution role with CloudWatch Logs access, or a dedicated function role with managed policy attachments and inline statements. An optional separate invoker role grants `lambda:InvokeFunction` to other services. |
| Networking | Optional VPC attachment with either existing security groups or a module-managed security group. Required `ec2:*` ENI permissions are attached automatically. |
| Storage | Optional Amazon EFS access point mount. |
| Logging | A dedicated CloudWatch log group with configurable retention, plus JSON/Text log format and per-level application and system log controls. |
| Observability | Optional AWS X-Ray tracing in `Active` or `PassThrough` mode. |
| Invocation | Lambda Function URLs with full CORS control, and aliases with weighted routing between versions. |
| Scheduling | One or many EventBridge Scheduler schedules, with flexible time windows, timezones, and custom payloads. |
| Event triggers | S3 bucket notifications, SQS event source mappings, and DynamoDB Streams mappings — each with filter criteria, and with the matching IAM permissions attached automatically. |
| Layers | Attach any number of Lambda layer versions. |

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy/releases).


This module is consumed through Terragrunt. Use the built-in `scaffold` command to bootstrap a new deployment
directory — it reads `.boilerplate/boilerplate.yml` from this repository and generates `terragrunt.hcl`,
`inputs.yaml`, and `local-tags.json` for you.

#### 1. Scaffold the deployment

```sh
# 1. Create and enter the target deployment directory
mkdir -p <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/lambda-my-function
cd <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/lambda-my-function

# 2. Scaffold the module (do NOT use --working-dir)
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy

# 3. Edit inputs.yaml with deployment-specific values
#    (all keys and comments are pre-populated from .boilerplate/inputs.yaml)
vi inputs.yaml

# 4. Apply
terragrunt apply
```

#### 2. Generated `terragrunt.hcl`

Scaffold produces the file below. It loads `inputs.yaml` as `local.local_vars` and merges the tag files from every
level of the hierarchy. `is_hub`, `org`, `spoke_def`, and `extra_tags` come from the hierarchy — never from
`inputs.yaml`.

```hcl
locals {
  local_vars  = yamldecode(file("./inputs.yaml"))
  spoke_vars  = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-inputs.yaml")))
  region_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-inputs.yaml")))
  env_vars    = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-inputs.yaml")))
  global_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-inputs.yaml")))

  local_tags  = jsondecode(file("./local-tags.json"))
  spoke_tags  = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-tags.json")))
  region_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-tags.json")))
  env_tags    = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-tags.json")))
  global_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-tags.json")))

  tags = merge(
    local.global_tags,
    local.env_tags,
    local.region_tags,
    local.spoke_tags,
    local.local_tags
  )
}

include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}

terraform {
  source = "github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy"
}

inputs = {
  is_hub           = false
  org              = local.env_vars.org
  spoke_def        = local.spoke_vars.spoke
  namespace        = local.local_vars.namespace
  repository_owner = local.local_vars.repository_owner
  release          = local.local_vars.release
  versions_bucket  = local.local_vars.versions_bucket
  lambda           = try(local.local_vars.lambda, {})
  absolute_path    = try(local.local_vars.absolute_path, "./")
  logs_bucket      = try(local.local_vars.logs_bucket, "")
  bucket_path      = try(local.local_vars.bucket_path, "")
  extra_tags       = local.tags
}
```

#### 3. Generated `inputs.yaml`

This is the file you edit. Every key below mirrors `.boilerplate/inputs.yaml`.

```yaml
# (Required) Namespace appended to the Lambda function name and its IAM resources.
# The function is named "<release.name>-<namespace>". Example: dev | uat | prod
namespace: "dev"

# (Required) Owner of the source code repository. Usually supplied by the CI/CD
# pipeline for traceability; reserved for future use and not referenced by any
# resource today. Example: cloudopsworks
repository_owner: "cloudopsworks"

# (Required) Release metadata for the deployed artifact.
release:
  name: "my-function" # (Required) Base name for the function and its IAM roles/policies.
  source:
    version: "1.0.0"  # (Required) Artifact version, rendered into the function description.

# (Required) Name of the S3 bucket holding the packaged application versions.
# The module reads the deployment ZIP from this bucket.
versions_bucket: "my-artifacts-bucket"

# (Optional) S3 object key of the deployment package inside versions_bucket.
# Default: ""
bucket_path: "releases/my-function/1.0.0/function.zip"

# (Optional) S3 bucket for application logs. Supplied by the CI/CD pipeline;
# reserved for future use and not referenced by any resource today. Default: ""
logs_bucket: ""

# (Optional) Absolute path to the Lambda function sources on the runner.
# Supplied by the CI/CD pipeline; reserved for future use and not referenced by
# any resource today. Default: "./"
absolute_path: "./"

# (Required) AWS Lambda function configuration. Default: {}
lambda:
  handler: "index.handler"   # (Required) Function entrypoint, e.g. "index.handler" (Node.js/Python) or "com.example.App::handleRequest" (Java).
  runtime: "nodejs22.x"      # (Required) Runtime identifier. Valid values include: nodejs18.x, nodejs20.x, nodejs22.x, python3.10, python3.11, python3.12, python3.13, java17, java21, dotnet8, ruby3.3, provided.al2023.
  #memory_size: 128          # (Optional) Memory in MB. Valid range 128-10240. Default: 128
  #timeout: 3                # (Optional) Execution timeout in seconds. Valid range 1-900. Default: 3
  #reserved_concurrency: -1  # (Optional) Reserved concurrent executions. -1 means unreserved (account pool). Default: -1
  #provisioned_concurrency: 0 # (Optional) Provisioned concurrent executions on the published version. Set > 0 to enable. Default: 0 (disabled)
  #log_retention_days: 14    # (Optional) CloudWatch log retention in days. Valid values: 1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1096, 1827, 2192, 2557, 2922, 3288, 3653, 0 (never expire). Default: 14

  ##
  # (Required) Environment variables passed to the function.
  # Use an empty list to declare none.
  environment:
    variables: []
    #  - name: "LOG_LEVEL"   # (Required) Environment variable name.
    #    value: "INFO"       # (Required) Environment variable value.

  ##
  # (Required) Lambda Function URL endpoints. Use an empty list to create none.
  functionUrls: []
  #  - id: "prod"                     # (Required) Unique key for the endpoint within this module.
  #    qualifier: "prod"              # (Required) Alias or version to expose. Empty string targets the unpublished "$LATEST".
  #    authorization_type: "AWS_IAM"  # (Required) Authorization model. Valid values: AWS_IAM, NONE. Empty string resolves to NONE.
  #    cors:                          # (Required) CORS block. Use {} to accept the defaults below.
  #      allowCredentials: false      # (Optional) Allow cookies/credentials on cross-origin requests. Default: false
  #      allowMethods: []             # (Optional) Allowed HTTP methods, e.g. ["GET", "POST"] or ["*"]. Default: []
  #      allowOrigins: []             # (Optional) Allowed origins, e.g. ["https://example.com"] or ["*"]. Default: []
  #      allowHeaders: []             # (Optional) Allowed request headers. Default: []
  #      exposeHeaders: []            # (Optional) Response headers exposed to the browser. Default: []
  #      maxAge: 600                  # (Optional) Preflight cache duration in seconds. Valid range 0-86400. Default: 600

  ##
  # (Optional) Alias pointing at the version published by this module.
  # Default: disabled
  #alias:
  #  enabled: true             # (Optional) Create the alias. Default: false
  #  name: "prod"              # (Required when enabled) Alias name, e.g. prod | uat | dev | demo
  #  routing_config:           # (Optional) Weighted routing to a second version. Default: [] (all traffic to the published version)
  #    - version: "1"          # (Required) Additional Lambda version to receive traffic.
  #      weight: 0.1           # (Required) Fraction of traffic for that version. Valid range 0.0-1.0.

  ##
  # (Optional) Lambda layers to attach. Default: []
  layers: []
  #  - arn: "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:layer:my-layer:1" # (Required) Fully qualified layer version ARN.

  ##
  # (Optional) VPC attachment for the function. Default: disabled
  vpc:
    enabled: false                # (Optional) Attach the function to a VPC. Default: false
    create_security_group: false  # (Optional) Create a managed security group allowing all egress. Default: false
    subnets: []                   # (Required when enabled) Subnet IDs for the ENIs, e.g. ["subnet-0abc...", "subnet-0def..."]
    security_groups: []           # (Required when enabled and create_security_group is false) Existing security group IDs, e.g. ["sg-0abc..."]

  ##
  # (Optional) Advanced CloudWatch logging configuration.
  #logging:
  #  log_format: "JSON"            # (Optional) Log output format. Valid values: JSON, Text. Default: JSON
  #  application_log_level: "INFO" # (Optional) Minimum level for application logs, only honored when log_format is JSON. Valid values: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL. Default: AWS default
  #  system_log_level: "INFO"      # (Optional) Minimum level for Lambda system logs, only honored when log_format is JSON. Valid values: DEBUG, INFO, WARN. Default: AWS default

  ##
  # (Optional) AWS X-Ray tracing. Default: disabled
  tracing: {}
  #  enabled: true    # (Optional) Enable X-Ray tracing. Default: false

  ##

  # Default: disabled (AWS default of 512 MB)
  #ephemeral_storage:
  #  enabled: true    # (Optional) Override the default ephemeral storage size. Default: false
```

## Quick Start

1. Package your Lambda function as a ZIP file and upload it to the S3 versions bucket used by your organization.
   Note the bucket name and the object key — they become `versions_bucket` and `bucket_path`.
2. Create the deployment directory inside your Terragrunt hierarchy and enter it:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/lambda-my-function
   cd <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/lambda-my-function
   ```
3. Scaffold the module:
   ```sh
   terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-lambda-deploy
   ```
4. Edit the generated `inputs.yaml`:
   - Set `namespace`, `repository_owner`, and `release` (`name` and `source.version`).
   - Set `versions_bucket` and `bucket_path` to point at your uploaded package.
   - Set `lambda.handler` and `lambda.runtime`.
   - Add any `lambda.environment.variables` your function needs, and leave `lambda.functionUrls: []`
     unless you want a public or IAM-authorized HTTPS endpoint.
   - Uncomment only the optional blocks you actually need — every block is documented inline.
5. Review the planned changes:
   ```sh
   terragrunt plan
   ```
6. Apply:
   ```sh
   terragrunt apply
   ```
7. Retrieve the function identifiers for downstream modules:
   ```sh
   terragrunt output function_arn
   terragrunt output function_invoke_arn
   ```

> **Note:** `is_hub`, `org`, `spoke_def`, and `extra_tags` are supplied by the Terragrunt hierarchy
> (`env-inputs.yaml`, `spoke-inputs.yaml`, and the merged tag files). Do not set them in `inputs.yaml`.


## Examples

All examples below are the `inputs.yaml` produced by `terragrunt scaffold`, edited for a specific scenario.

#### Minimal function

The smallest working configuration. Creates the function, a default execution role with CloudWatch Logs
access, and a log group with 14-day retention.

```yaml
namespace: "dev"
repository_owner: "cloudopsworks"
release:
  name: "hello-world"
  source:
    version: "1.0.0"
versions_bucket: "acme-artifacts-use1"
bucket_path: "releases/hello-world/1.0.0/function.zip"
lambda:
  handler: "index.handler"
  runtime: "nodejs22.x"
  environment:
    variables:
      - name: "LOG_LEVEL"
        value: "INFO"
  functionUrls: []
```

#### VPC-attached API handler with a Function URL

Attaches the function to private subnets with a module-managed security group, grants it read access to an S3
bucket, and exposes an IAM-authorized Function URL. The `ec2:*` ENI permissions required for VPC attachment are
added automatically.

```yaml
namespace: "prod"
repository_owner: "cloudopsworks"
release:
  name: "api-handler"
  source:
    version: "2.1.0"
versions_bucket: "acme-artifacts-use1"
bucket_path: "releases/api-handler/2.1.0/function.zip"
lambda:
  handler: "api.handler"
  runtime: "nodejs22.x"
  memory_size: 512
  timeout: 30
  log_retention_days: 30
  environment:
    variables:
      - name: "NODE_ENV"
        value: "production"
  vpc:
    enabled: true
    create_security_group: true
    subnets:
      - "subnet-0a1b2c3d4e5f60718"
      - "subnet-0a1b2c3d4e5f60719"
  iam:
    enabled: true
    statements:
      - effect: "Allow"
        action:
          - "s3:GetObject"
          - "s3:ListBucket"
        resource:
          - "arn:aws:s3:::acme-uploads"
          - "arn:aws:s3:::acme-uploads/*"
  tracing:
    enabled: true
    mode: "Active"
  functionUrls:
    - id: "prod"
      qualifier: ""
      authorization_type: "AWS_IAM"
      cors:
        allowCredentials: true
        allowMethods:
          - "GET"
          - "POST"
        allowOrigins:
          - "https://app.example.com"
        allowHeaders:
          - "content-type"
          - "authorization"
        maxAge: 86400
```

#### Scheduled job

Runs the function hourly through EventBridge Scheduler. Scheduling requires `iam.execRole.enabled: true` —
the module adds `scheduler.amazonaws.com` to the invoker role's trust policy automatically.

```yaml
namespace: "prod"
repository_owner: "cloudopsworks"
release:
  name: "nightly-report"
  source:
    version: "1.4.2"
versions_bucket: "acme-artifacts-use1"
bucket_path: "releases/nightly-report/1.4.2/function.zip"
lambda:
  handler: "com.example.Report::handleRequest"
  runtime: "java21"
  memory_size: 1024
  timeout: 900
  environment:
    variables: []
  functionUrls: []
  iam:
    enabled: true
    execRole:
      enabled: true
  schedule:
    enabled: true
    expression: "cron(0 3 * * ? *)"
    timezone: "America/Bogota"
    suspended: false
    flexible:
      enabled: true
      maxWindow: 20
    payload:
      mode: "full"
      notify: true
```

#### SQS-triggered worker

Consumes an existing SQS queue with a filter on the message body. The SQS read permissions are attached to the
function role automatically when `iam.enabled` is true.

```yaml
namespace: "prod"
repository_owner: "cloudopsworks"
release:
  name: "order-worker"
  source:
    version: "3.0.1"
versions_bucket: "acme-artifacts-use1"
bucket_path: "releases/order-worker/3.0.1/function.zip"
lambda:
  handler: "worker.handler"
  runtime: "python3.13"
  memory_size: 256
  timeout: 120
  reserved_concurrency: 20
  environment:
    variables:
      - name: "QUEUE_MODE"
        value: "batch"
  functionUrls: []
  iam:
    enabled: true
  triggers:
    sqs:
      queueName: "acme-orders"
      batchSize: 10
      maximumConcurrency: 5
      metricsConfig: true
      filterCriteria:
        - pattern_object:
            body:
              Location:
                - "New York"
```

```
Available targets:

  help                                Help screen
  help/all                            Display help for all targets
  help/short                          This help short screen
  init/%                              Initialize the project for a specific cloud provider: %S
  lint                                Lint terraform/opentofu code
  tag                                 Tag the current version

```

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
|------|-------------|------|---------|:--------:|
| <a name="input_absolute_path"></a> [absolute\_path](#input\_absolute\_path) | (Optional) Absolute path to the Lambda function sources on the runner. Supplied by the CI/CD pipeline; reserved for future use and not currently referenced by any resource. Default: "./" | `string` | `"./"` | no |
| <a name="input_bucket_path"></a> [bucket\_path](#input\_bucket\_path) | (Optional) S3 object key of the deployment package inside versions\_bucket, e.g. "releases/my-function/1.0.0/function.zip". Default: "" | `string` | `""` | no |
| <a name="input_extra_tags"></a> [extra\_tags](#input\_extra\_tags) | Extra tags to add to the resources | `map(string)` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_is_hub"></a> [is\_hub](#input\_is\_hub) | Is this a hub or spoke configuration? | `bool` | `false` | no |
| <a name="input_lambda"></a> [lambda](#input\_lambda) | (Required) AWS Lambda function configuration. Supports runtime settings, environment variables, function URLs, aliases, layers, VPC and EFS attachment, logging, X-Ray tracing, IAM roles, EventBridge schedules, and S3/SQS/DynamoDB triggers. See the inline documentation above for every supported attribute. Default: {} | `any` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_logs_bucket"></a> [logs\_bucket](#input\_logs\_bucket) | (Optional) Name of the S3 bucket for application logs. Supplied by the CI/CD pipeline; reserved for future use and not currently referenced by any resource. Default: "" | `string` | `""` | no |
| <a name="input_namespace"></a> [namespace](#input\_namespace) | (Required) Namespace appended to the Lambda function name and its IAM resources, e.g. "dev". Combined with release.name to form the function name "<release.name>-<namespace>". | `string` | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_org"></a> [org](#input\_org) | Organization details | <pre>object({<br/>    organization_name = string<br/>    organization_unit = string<br/>    environment_type  = string<br/>    environment_name  = string<br/>  })</pre> | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_release"></a> [release](#input\_release) | (Required) Release metadata for the deployed artifact. Requires release.name (base name for the function and its IAM resources) and release.source.version (artifact version shown in the function description). | `any` | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_repository_owner"></a> [repository\_owner](#input\_repository\_owner) | (Required) Owner of the source code repository, e.g. "cloudopsworks". Supplied by the CI/CD pipeline for traceability; reserved for future use and not currently referenced by any resource. | `string` | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_spoke_def"></a> [spoke\_def](#input\_spoke\_def) | Spoke ID Number, must be a 3 digit number | `string` | `"001"` | no |
| <a name="input_versions_bucket"></a> [versions\_bucket](#input\_versions\_bucket) | (Required) Name of the S3 bucket holding the packaged application versions. The module reads the deployment ZIP from this bucket. | `string` | n/a | yes |

## Outputs

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| <a name="output_function_arn"></a> [function\_arn](#output\_function\_arn) | Unqualified ARN of the deployed Lambda function. |
| <a name="output_function_invoke_arn"></a> [function\_invoke\_arn](#output\_function\_invoke\_arn) | ARN to be used by API Gateway and other integrations to invoke the Lambda function. |
| <a name="output_function_name"></a> [function\_name](#output\_function\_name) | Name of the deployed Lambda function, formed as "<release.name>-<namespace>". |
| <a name="output_lambda_exec_role"></a> [lambda\_exec\_role](#output\_lambda\_exec\_role) | Name of the IAM invoker role granting lambda:InvokeFunction on this function. Empty string when lambda.iam.execRole.enabled is false. |
| <a name="output_lambda_exec_role_arn"></a> [lambda\_exec\_role\_arn](#output\_lambda\_exec\_role\_arn) | ARN of the IAM invoker role granting lambda:InvokeFunction on this function. Empty string when lambda.iam.execRole.enabled is false. |
| <a name="output_lambda_function_role"></a> [lambda\_function\_role](#output\_lambda\_function\_role) | Name of the IAM role assumed by the Lambda function at runtime. Returns the dedicated function role when lambda.iam.enabled is true, otherwise the default role created by this module. |
| <a name="output_lambda_function_role_arn"></a> [lambda\_function\_role\_arn](#output\_lambda\_function\_role\_arn) | ARN of the IAM role assumed by the Lambda function at runtime. Returns the dedicated function role when lambda.iam.enabled is true, otherwise the default role created by this module. |
